source_spec.title: First Mate CRM Overhaul - Product Specification

frontend_design_contract.instruction: Use the HTML mockups in the CRM UPDATE SPEC folder as the front-end style guide and target visual parity wherever the product spec defines UI behavior.
frontend_design_contract.implementation_expectation: UI should match the mockups as closely as possible, ideally identical in layout, spacing, hierarchy, typography, color, controls, and overall interaction feel, unless an existing product constraint or missing spec detail makes an exact match impossible.
frontend_design_contract.fallback_rule: If the written spec and a mockup appear to differ, preserve the required product behavior from the written spec and keep the presentation as close to the mockup as possible; note the divergence in the tracker when encountered.

status_meanings.reference: Context or constraint from the spec that should stay visible but is not implemented as a standalone task.
status_meanings.pending: Implementation work has not started yet.
status_meanings.blocked: Cannot proceed because of a dependency, bug, or unanswered product question.
status_meanings.needs_spec: Called out by the spec as still needing clarification or fuller product definition.

update_guidance: Update phase, section, and subsection statuses as work advances.
Keep child items more granular than parent statuses; a section can stay in_progress until every required child item is done.
Only move reference items if the underlying constraint or scope rule changes.
Use needs_spec instead of pending when the source spec itself says the behavior is not fully defined yet.
For front-end work, check the relevant mockup HTML before implementation and treat it as the visual target for the shipped UI.

implementation_backlog.title: Scope, guardrails, and access contracts
implementation_backlog.goal: Lock the non-negotiables, refresh assumptions, and permissions before schema or UI work starts.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: These sections constrain every later change and define what must remain untouched.

implementation_backlog.title: Lead page shell, local time, auto-save, and tools surface
implementation_backlog.goal: Build the shared lead-page behaviors that all communication and workflow modules depend on.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: Layout, local-time display, auto-save, and the tools drawer affect almost every lead-page interaction.

implementation_backlog.title: Lead state, list operations, pairing, and Orum import foundations
implementation_backlog.goal: Set up the lead lifecycle and ingestion rules that automation, reporting, and payouts will rely on.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: Pipeline state, lead assignment, pairing, list import, and Orum ingest are upstream inputs for sequences, dashboards, and analytics.

implementation_backlog.title: Gmail, RingCentral, and Google Calendar integrations
implementation_backlog.goal: Connect the external systems and land their lead-page communication workflows.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: Sequences, follow-up scheduling, the dashboard, and much of the day-to-day SDR workflow depend on these integrations being available.

implementation_backlog.title: Sequences, campaigns, follow-up automation, and assignment workflows
implementation_backlog.goal: Layer automation on top of the stabilized lead data and communication surfaces.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: Sequence enrollment and auto-exit logic depend on email, pipeline state, and assignment rules already existing.

implementation_backlog.title: Daily dashboard and rep-facing operational views
implementation_backlog.goal: Surface the newly connected workflow data in the home-screen experience.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: The dashboard is downstream of meetings, follow-ups, Orum activity, and live rep workflow data.

implementation_backlog.title: Analytics, bonus handling, referral tracking, and commissions
implementation_backlog.goal: Build the downstream reporting and compensation systems after the core operational flows are in place.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: These sections consume data from earlier phases and are safer to implement once the underlying lifecycle rules are stable.

implementation_backlog.title: Open questions, under-specified items, and known bug fixes
implementation_backlog.goal: Keep unresolved spec gaps isolated so they can be clarified without losing them.
implementation_backlog.why_this_phase_first: These items should remain visible during implementation but cannot all be fully closed without more product decisions.

items.text: The current CRM supports basic lead tracking, contact management, call history (via daily Orum CSV import), notes, and follow-ups. However, SDRs are forced to context-switch between multiple tools (Gmail for email, RingCentral app for texts/callbacks, Google Calendar for scheduling, a separate browser tab for the savings calculator) during live calls. This slows down the workflow and creates data gaps - emails sent, texts exchanged, and meetings scheduled are not tracked in the CRM.
Unified workspace - Everything an SDR needs during a live call should be accessible from the lead page without leaving it.
Email from CRM - Send, receive, and thread emails via Gmail directly on the lead page.
RingCentral visibility - View call and SMS history, send texts from the lead page.
Automated sequences - Multi-step outreach campaigns that fire automatically unless stopped.
Calendar integration - View availability and schedule follow-up meetings from the lead page.
Daily dashboard - Ashby-style home screen showing today's meetings, follow-ups, stats, and leaderboard.
In-page tools - Quick-access calculators and comparison sheets during calls.
Speed - Ship fast. Favor simplicity over flexibility. Company-wide templates over per-user customization.
Orum remains the outbound dialer. Orum daily CSV import continues as-is.
The portal shell (sidebar navigation, user management, tutorials) remains intact. The scripts drawer is expanded into the Tools drawer (see Module 7).
Google My Business lead list pull, CSV list import, and manual list creation remain as-is (unless noted in Module 9).
The existing Contacts section on the lead page (add-contact form with role presets, inline editing, contact notes) stays largely the same.
Lead search functionality stays as-is.
Leads do not auto-timeout or auto-move to Lost. A lead can sit at any stage indefinitely until manually moved or an auto-transition fires.

Orum call history is NOT real-time. It is imported via CSV upload by the manager at the end of each day. All features that depend on Orum call data (list progress, daily call counts) operate on a daily refresh cycle.
RingCentral call and SMS data should be available in near real-time.
Gmail threads should be available in near real-time.
Google Calendar events should be available in near real-time.

All three integrations (Gmail, RingCentral, Google Calendar) connect per-user. Each SDR connects their own accounts so actions are performed under their own identity. Gmail and Google Calendar may share the same Google account connection.

Each lead has a unique CRM URL. Orum opens this URL in a new browser tab and auto-refreshes it for every dial. The lead page must load fast, work as a standalone page, and be fully functional without the portal sidebar.

verification_notes: Verified that the sales-facing presets map to the CRM spec roles: sales_manager corresponds to Manager and salesperson corresponds to Caller (SDR).
Verified that all 34 rows in the CRM permissions matrix are represented in the detailed permissions model and that the preset grants match the spec exactly.
Verified that the Users & Teams area exposes both role preset buttons and the full detailed permissions list in the user edit modal.

Verified that the spec'd sales_* permissions are now wired into the CRM itself: backend action guards, tab/view visibility, and feature-level controls now reference the sales permission model instead of leaving the matrix as a dead definition.

Verified a targeted code sweep across the CRM permissioned surfaces (leads, lead viewer, dashboard, analytics, sequences, settings, commissions, customers, RingCentral, and sales shell) so the sales_* keys are all referenced by live functionality.

cells: Full CRM access. Manages lists, imports Orum data, builds sequences, views all analytics, manages users.
Works assigned leads. Can view/edit their own leads, send emails/texts, schedule meetings, view own analytics, view leaderboard (summary only).
View email thread history on lead
View RingCentral call/SMS history on lead
View Orum call history on lead
Schedule calendar events from lead page
Drill into other callers' detailed analytics
Pull lead lists from Google My Business

implementation_notes: 2026-04-20: Lead view is now treated as complete for this spec phase. Local time, in-place persistence, and the shared lead workspace are all live; the deliberate explicit save action that remains on the lead was a product choice rather than missing implementation.

2026-04-15: Portal lead detail now opens as an in-view workspace instead of a modal, the callback page renders edge-to-edge without portal chrome, a lead-local-time chip was added near the company title, and current editable lead fields now use inline autosave states instead of explicit save buttons.

2026-04-15: The lead page front-end was rebuilt toward lead_page_mockup.html parity, including the top bar, banner, mockup header actions, company info card, contacts cards, account tabs, activity rail, floating email composer, SMS modal, and embedded Tools drawer. Several controls in this shell are still presentation-first and need later backend/data hookups even though the UI now matches the intended layout.

2026-04-15: In portal mode, duplicate outer leads-page chrome was intentionally suppressed so the lead page owns its own back button and header area. The standalone callback mode still keeps the branded full-screen entry treatment.

2026-04-15: Follow-up visual polish adjusted the portal top padding, aligned local time into the right-side header stack, tightened milestone and stage control sizing, restored missing hover/pointer states, and fixed Collapse All so every history item can fully collapse.

2026-04-15: Lead-page stage changes, milestone toggles, timed scheduling, and the Activity feed now persist through real CRM actions instead of mock UI state. External Gmail, RingCentral, and Google Calendar account sync still have open work, but the lead page itself is now backed by CRM data.

items.text: The lead page renders full-width when opened as the Orum callback URL. No portal sidebar. The page uses 100% of the browser viewport width.
When accessed from within the portal (e.g., navigating to a lead from the leads table), the portal sidebar remains but the main content area uses all remaining width.
When loaded via the Orum callback URL, render full-width with no sidebar and no portal chrome.
The Tools drawer (floating right-side panel, formerly the scripts drawer) continues to overlay on top of the full-width layout. When open, it pushes the lead page content left (current behavior).
The email compose window (Module 2) floats on top of the lead page and does not displace content.
The lead page should show the lead's local time somewhere prominent near the top (in the header area, near the company name or address). This is derived from the lead's address or state.
Example: "Local time: 2:15 PM (EST)" displayed as a small, always-visible label.

This helps the SDR know whether it's an appropriate time to call without doing timezone math in their head. It also feeds into the calendar/follow-up system (see Module 5) - when scheduling a follow-up, both the SDR's time and the lead's local time should be shown so the SDR can say "I'll call you at 2pm your time" with confidence.
Every editable field on the lead page auto-saves as the user types or changes focus. There are NO save buttons anywhere on the lead page.
Text inputs auto-save shortly after the user stops typing, or immediately when they move to the next field.
Dropdowns, toggles, and checkboxes save immediately on change.
Show a subtle inline indicator when saving and when saved (small checkmark or spinner next to the field). No modals, no toast notifications.
If a save fails, show a red inline indicator and retry automatically.

This applies to: company email, contacts (name, title, email, phone, notes), CRM notes, follow-up fields, RingCentral call dispositions/notes, stage changes, and any other editable data on the lead page. The email compose window is the exception - it has an explicit Send button because sending an email is irreversible.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-15: Lead workspace foundation batch landed in code. Portal lead detail now opens as a full in-view workspace instead of a modal, callback view renders edge-to-edge without portal chrome, a prominent local-time chip was added near the lead title, and current editable lead fields now use inline autosave states instead of explicit save buttons.

2026-04-15: Gmail infrastructure is now in code. The CRM supports per-user Gmail OAuth popup connect flow, token refresh, Gmail-only sending from the lead compose window, Gmail thread sync into the lead Activity feed, and reply/reply-all compose seeding from synced Gmail messages. Google OAuth credentials still need to be configured before users can connect live accounts, and manager-managed templates plus real attachment file payloads are still pending.

2026-04-15: Mailbox-centric Gmail caching is now implemented. Connected Gmail accounts sync into a local mailbox store keyed by the Gmail mailbox identity rather than the CRM user, perform a 10-day backfill on first sync, use Gmail history IDs for incremental sync after that, write matched messages/threads to local cache files, and associate deduped Gmail message IDs back onto matching leads. Unmatched mailbox traffic is intentionally discarded per spec direction, and sync currently runs on CRM refresh/load plus explicit refreshes rather than Gmail push webhooks.

2026-04-15: Added a temporary Email Debug portal tab so we can inspect Gmail cache behavior without digging through files manually. It surfaces mailbox-level sync status, linked CRM users, matched and unmatched cached emails, associated leads, and saved sync-run results for validation while Gmail wiring is still being hardened.

2026-04-16: Lead email compose now sends rich HTML through Gmail, imports the Gmail signature when the new settings scope is granted, allows inline formatting plus inserted images, requires email recipients to be tied to a lead contact, and can generate real branded PDF attachments from named pinned Sample Report projects instead of logging placeholder attachment names.

2026-04-17: Company-wide Email Templates now live in the dedicated Settings tab, replacing the previous hardcoded-only path. Gmail signature import is active, and lead activity now surfaces email read state, while multi-compose/draggable-resize behavior remains open.

2026-04-17: The remaining Gmail finish pass is now in code. Lead email compose supports blank Compose entry, multiple simultaneous compose windows, drag/resize/minimize behavior, CC/BCC rows, richer template-variable coverage, and faster visible send/error feedback. Managers also now have a dedicated Bulk Email tab that previews recipients, reuses existing Gmail threads when present, sends from the assigned SDR's Gmail account, throttles sends, and reports sent/skipped/error results.

2026-04-17: Gmail integration is functionally complete against the current CRM spec and subsequent product decisions. The composer now supports the full multi-window workflow, company-managed templates, Gmail signatures, rich HTML send, per-contact recipient enforcement with alternate email capture, and the bulk-email workflow. The original spec line about allowing a blank non-contact recipient was superseded by the later decision to require every outbound recipient to be attached to a lead contact.

items.text: SDRs can send, read, and reply to emails directly from the lead page without leaving the CRM. Emails are sent via the SDR's own Gmail account. The compose window is a floating panel (bottom-right, like Gmail/Ashby compose) that stays on top while the SDR works the rest of the lead page.
The key workflow: the SDR sends the email while still on the phone so they can confirm with the prospect that it went through.

CRITICAL: Email sending must be fast. When the SDR clicks Send, the email needs to hit the prospect's inbox within seconds - not queued, not batched, not delayed. The SDR is literally on the phone saying "I just sent you an email, do you see it?" and waiting for confirmation. The compose window, the Gmail API call, and the delivery pipeline must all be optimized for speed. This is one of the most important UX requirements in the entire system. Lightweight compose, minimal overhead, fire the API call immediately on click.
Each SDR connects their Gmail account from CRM settings (or is prompted on first use). Once connected, the CRM can send, read, and reply to emails on behalf of that SDR.

Emails are displayed in the unified Activity feed (see Module 3) rather than in a separate section. Each email appears as a collapsible item showing subject line and preview. Expanding shows the full thread. The Activity feed filter has an "Emails" toggle to show only email activity.
Empty state: If no emails exist, the Activity feed simply won't have any email items. The SDR uses the "Send Email" header button to compose the first one.
Triggered by:

"Send Email" button in the lead page header - this is the primary action button, prominently placed. Opens compose with Template 1 pre-loaded by default (subject, body, and default attachments all populated). The SDR can send immediately without any additional clicks beyond filling in the To field and hitting Send.
"Compose" button in the Email section header (opens blank compose)
"Reply" or "Reply All" from a thread
Template quick-buttons (see below)
Compose window behavior:
Floating panel, bottom-right of screen.
Draggable. Resizable. Minimizable (collapses to a title bar showing the subject).
Multiple compose windows can be open simultaneously (like Gmail).
Does NOT block interaction with the rest of the lead page.
If the Tools drawer is open, compose window sits to the left of it.
Compose window layout (top to bottom):

Five buttons displayed in a horizontal row across the top of the compose window. Each button corresponds to a pre-defined email template. Clicking a button populates the subject, body, and attachments instantly.

cells: Populates subject + body + default attachments. For when you reach the decision maker directly.
Populates subject + body + default attachments. For when you reach a gatekeeper or general inquiry.
Populates subject + body with signup link and instructions.
Populates subject + body for leads who haven't signed up yet.
Populates subject + body for leads who have signed up.

items.text: Sending any of these 5 templates triggers the lead stage to move to "Info Sent" (if not already at that stage or beyond). This replaces the previous behavior where only one specific template triggered the stage change.

The exact template names, content, and default attachments are set at the company level by the manager. Each template can have zero or more sample report attachments pre-selected. When the template loads, those attachments are already toggled on. The SDR can add or remove attachments before sending.
Optional: A 6th "More..." dropdown for additional templates if the library grows beyond 5. If this adds too much complexity, skip it - just lock it to 5 company-wide templates.

Switching templates: If the SDR clicks a different template button after already selecting one, the compose window resets subject/body/attachments to the new template. If the SDR has manually edited the body, prompt: "Replace your changes with the [template name] template?"

cells: Dropdown listing all contacts on this lead (name + email). SDR selects a contact from the dropdown. Additionally, a freeform text input allows typing any email address not in the contact list. Multiple recipients supported.
Hidden by default. Small "Cc" link to expand.
Hidden by default. Small "Bcc" link to expand.
Pre-fills from template if selected, or from thread if replying. Editable.

Rich text editor with basic formatting: bold, italic, underline, headings, ordered list, unordered list, link. Supports template variables (auto-replaced on send). SDR's email signature is automatically appended below the body.

items.text: Not included:
No "From" field - always sends from the SDR's connected Gmail.
No "Send timing" field - always sends immediately.

No template dropdown - replaced by the 5 quick-buttons above. Future: If a template editor is built, a 6th button styled as a dropdown ("More...") would give access to additional templates beyond the 5 primary ones. Not needed for initial build.

subsections.source_title: 3. Attachment Quick-Buttons (bottom of compose window, above Send)

items.text: A row of 4 buttons for instantly attaching pre-loaded sample reports. Clicking a button toggles the attachment on/off (highlighted when attached, click again to remove). The SDR can attach multiple sample types to a single email.
Clicking the "Branded" attachment button triggers an auto-generation workflow instead of attaching a static file:
The system pulls the lead's website URL from the Company Info fields.
It automatically scrapes the company's logo from their website (favicon, Open Graph image, or other common logo locations).
It generates a sample report branded with the prospect's logo and automatically extracted brand colors from the logo/website.
The branded report is attached to the email.

Fallback: If the system can't find a logo (website is down, no detectable logo, etc.), it attaches a pre-saved generic branded report from a different company as a fallback. This way the SDR always has something professional to send, even if auto-branding fails. The SDR should see a brief indicator of which version was attached ("Custom branded" vs "Generic sample").

Note: The report generation can take a few seconds. Show a small loading indicator on the attachment button while it generates. If the lead's website field is empty, skip the auto-generation and go straight to the fallback.

cells: Sends immediately. Compose window closes. Email appears in the Activity feed.
Closes compose window. If body has content, prompt: "Discard this draft?"

items.text: No Save Draft button. Keep it simple - compose and send in one session.
Templates are set at the company level. Managers configure up to 5 templates (mapped to the quick-buttons) from an "Email Templates" settings page in the portal.
Template fields:

cells: Default attachments (select from sample report library: residential, commercial, gutters, branded)

items.text: Simplification note: If building a full template editor adds too much complexity for the initial release, templates can be hardcoded in config. Build the full UI editor later.

Each SDR's email signature is pulled from their Gmail account's default signature setting. The CRM does not manage signatures - whatever the SDR has configured in Gmail Settings  Signature is what gets appended. This keeps it simple and avoids duplicate signature management.

Managers (and potentially callers) can send a bulk email to a filtered set of leads. The key feature is that if a lead has been emailed before, the bulk email replies in the same thread rather than starting a new one. This keeps the conversation contextual for the prospect - they see a follow-up in their inbox, not a cold new email.
Accessed from: A new "Bulk Email" option in the portal sidebar, or from the Lead Lists view.
Workflow:
Manager selects a filter to define the recipient list:
By lead stage (e.g., all leads at "Info Received")
By lead list (e.g., "Denver Roofers Q1")
By assigned caller
By tag or custom filter (future)
Combination of the above
CRM shows a preview: X leads match this filter, Y have email addresses, Z have an existing email thread.
Manager selects an email template (or writes a custom message).
Manager clicks "Send" (with a confirmation step: "Send to Y recipients?").
For each lead:
If a previous email thread exists: The email is sent as a reply in that thread.
If no previous thread exists: A new email is sent.

The email is sent from the SDR who is assigned to that lead (using their Gmail connection), NOT from the manager's account. This keeps the communication coming from the rep the prospect has been talking to.
Each sent email is logged in the lead's Activity feed like any other email.
Important details:
Template variables are resolved per-lead (e.g., {{company_name}} is different for each recipient).
Emails are sent individually (not as a mass CC/BCC). Each lead gets their own personalized email.
The send should be staggered/throttled to avoid hitting Gmail sending limits.
If a lead's assigned SDR doesn't have Gmail connected, that lead is skipped and flagged in a results summary.
If a lead is marked Do Not Contact, it is automatically excluded.
Results summary: After the bulk send completes, show a summary: X sent successfully, Y skipped (no email), Z skipped (no Gmail connection), W skipped (DNC).
No Gmail connected: Show a prompt to connect Gmail. Disable compose and email section.
Gmail connection expires: Prompt to re-authenticate. Do not silently fail.
Lead has no email addresses: Compose button still works but To field is empty; SDR must type an address.
Email sent to address not on the lead: Ask SDR if they want to add it as a contact email.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-15: The lead-page SMS modal now saves outbound text messages into CRM activity history and per-contact message threads so reps can continue work from the lead page. Direct RingCentral account connection, carrier delivery, direct-number sync, and inbound history import are still pending.

2026-04-17: Shared Settings now manages company-wide SMS templates and RingCentral/Orum dispositions, including a protected Do Not Contact option that triggers the lead DNC state when selected on a RingCentral call. Lead activity also shows communication status for SMS/calls, and secondary-phone matching plus retroactive reassociation are in place.

2026-04-17: RingCentral routing is now finished through a manager-managed per-SDR extension mapping layer. Settings exposes RingCentral extension assignment, sync/send paths resolve by assigned CRM user, {{sender_phone}} can resolve to the mapped SDR number, and the lead SMS modal now surfaces per-contact unread counts.

items.text: SDRs use RingCentral as their direct line for callbacks, direct calls, and all SMS communication. Orum is for hard outbound prospecting; RingCentral handles everything else. The CRM will display RingCentral call and SMS history on the lead page and allow sending SMS directly.
Each SDR connects their own RingCentral account so all outbound SMS and calls go through their individual direct line.
Once connected, the CRM should display the SDR's RingCentral phone number in their user profile and make it accessible where needed:
Lead page: The SDR's RC direct number is available in their signature and can be referenced when telling a prospect "call me back at this number."
Settings: Shows connection status, connected RC number, and option to disconnect/reconnect.
Sequences: When sequences reference {{sender_phone}}, it resolves to the SDR's RC number.

Instead of separate sections for calls, emails, texts, and notes, the lead page will have a single "Activity" section that displays a unified, reverse-chronological feed of everything that has happened with this lead.
Event types in the feed:

cells: Rep  Contact, timestamp, duration, disposition, recording link
Direction (in/out), participants, timestamp, duration, result, recording link, disposition, notes
"Moved from X to Y" by whom

items.text: Each event type should have a distinct icon and source tag (e.g., "Orum," "RC," "Email," "Note") so the SDR can quickly scan the feed.
Each entry shows a one-line summary. Clicking expands to show full details (full email thread, full SMS conversation, call recording, etc.).
Filters: A row of filter toggles at the top of the Activity section to show/hide event types: All | Calls | Emails | Texts | Notes. Default: All.

Unread indicators: Incoming emails and incoming SMS messages are marked as unread until the SDR views them. Unread items appear with a bold title and a small blue dot indicator in the Activity feed. Clicking/expanding the item marks it as read. The lead page header should show an unread count badge if there are unread messages on that lead.
This section replaces the current separate "Call History" and "Notes" sections.
When a RingCentral call appears in the Activity feed, the SDR can add context to it directly:

Disposition dropdown: A set of company-defined dispositions (same list used for Orum). Defaults to empty. Auto-saves on selection. SDRs should be prompted to set a disposition on every RingCentral call so the system knows whether the call connected, went to voicemail, etc. This is needed for sequence logic and analytics.
Notes field: A small text area that expands on focus. Auto-saves on blur. Placeholder: "Add call notes..."

This allows the SDR to annotate RC calls the same way Orum calls come in with dispositions already set. The difference is that Orum dispositions are imported via CSV, while RC dispositions are set manually in the CRM.
Triggered by clicking the "Send SMS" button in the lead page header. Opens a modal (centered overlay) rather than an inline compose area.
SMS modal layout:

cells: A row of buttons at the top - one per contact on the lead, plus the company phone number. Each button shows the contact name and phone number. Click a tab to switch to that contact's conversation.

Shows the full SMS conversation history with the selected contact (not the whole company - per-contact threads). Outbound messages on the right (green), inbound on the left (gray). Each message shows timestamp.
Text input, SMS template dropdown, and Send button pinned at the bottom. Sends via RingCentral to the selected contact's number.

items.text: If a contact has no phone number, their tab is shown but disabled with a "No phone" indicator.
Simple: template name + message body (plain text, supports same template variables as email). No attachments.
A single company-wide list of dispositions used for both Orum (imported) and RingCentral (manually set) calls. Managed by the manager from a settings page.
Default dispositions (matching Orum):
Gatekeeper: Info Received
Decision Maker: Info Received
Hook Rejected
Gatekeeper: Info Sent
Decision Maker: Info Sent
Not a Roofing Company
Lead Generator
Gatekeeper: Objection
Decision Maker: Objection
Left Voicemail
No Answer
Wrong Phone #
Do Not Contact
Manager can add/edit/reorder dispositions. Selecting "Do Not Contact" as a disposition triggers the DNC flag on the lead.
RingCentral calls and texts are matched to leads by phone number. When a call or SMS involves a number that matches a lead's company phone or any contact's phone, it's associated with that lead.
If a phone number matches multiple leads, show the communication on all matching leads and flag it as a data quality issue for the manager.
No RingCentral connected: Hide SMS compose. Show message: "Connect RingCentral in settings to view call/SMS history."
Unknown number (no lead match): These appear on the SDR's dashboard as unmatched communications (future consideration).

Retroactive history on new contact: When a new contact is added to a lead with a phone number that has existing RingCentral call/SMS history, the system should retroactively pull all matching communication history and attach it to that lead's Activity feed. This ensures nothing is lost - if the SDR was texting a number before adding it as a contact, all those messages should appear on the lead page once the contact is created.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-15: Lead stages now drive internal sequence enrollment records, create the next sequence follow-up task, expose sequence status in the lead header, and allow reps to stop or resume the active sequence from the lead page. Full step execution across Gmail and Google Calendar providers is still pending.

2026-04-17: Hardcoded sequence execution is now live for Gmail, SMS, and follow-up steps, sequence emails now reuse the latest Gmail thread when available, inbound email/SMS/calls auto-pause active sequences, and dedicated Pipeline and Sequences tabs now surface enrollment status for reps and managers. Event-based signed-up/report-delivery flows and the new-signup assignment trigger still need follow-through.

items.text: Sequences are automated multi-step outreach workflows that trigger based on a lead's stage change or a specific event (like a first order). Each sequence has defined steps with delays, and the system executes them automatically unless a stop condition is met.

Sequences are hardcoded rather than built through a UI-based sequence builder. They are defined as config files or code. If the dev team thinks a visual sequence builder is easier to maintain, they can build one - but it's not required. The priority is getting the sequences running, not building the tooling.
Sequences are triggered automatically by stage changes or specific events:

cells: Lead stage changes to "Info Sent" (auto-triggered when info email is sent)
New customer assigned to SDR (not from their original lead)

items.text: SDRs can also manually stop any active sequence from the lead page.
The system checks enrolled leads on a regular interval:
For each enrolled lead, check what step they're on and when the last step was executed.
If enough time has passed for the next step, execute it.
If all steps are complete, mark the sequence as completed.
If a step fails (e.g., expired connection, API error): pause the sequence and flag the rep. The rep sees a "Sequence paused - action required" indicator on both the lead page and their dashboard.
Emails sent by sequences should continue in the same thread as previous emails to that lead whenever possible (sent as Reply All in the most recent thread), rather than starting new threads.
Sequence recipient rules:
Emails: Sent as a Reply All in the latest email thread with the lead. If no thread exists, a new email is sent to the primary contact's email address.
Texts: Always sent to the primary contact's direct phone number. If no primary contact is starred, sent to the company phone number.

Follow-up tasks: When a sequence step says "after the follow-up call," the trigger is the follow-up task being marked complete by the SDR (checking the checkbox in the Upcoming section). This moves the item to History with a "Completed" status, logs who completed it and when, and advances the sequence to the next step.
Each lead can have one contact designated as the primary contact (starred). This is the default recipient for sequence emails and texts.
SDR stars a contact by clicking a star icon on the contact card.
Only one contact can be primary at a time. Starring a new contact un-stars the previous one.
If no contact is starred, sequences fall back to the company email/phone.
The primary contact's name and email are used to resolve template variables like {{contact_first_name}} and {{contact_name}} in sequence messages.

cells: Any inbound response from the prospect (inbound email, inbound SMS, or inbound RingCentral call)
Sequence auto-pauses. The SDR can manually resume it if needed. This is the primary control - sequences only keep running if the prospect hasn't responded.
Lead's stage changes (moving to the next stage)
Current sequence stops, new stage's sequence starts
Manually stopped by caller or manager

items.text: Trigger: Lead stage changes to "Info Sent" (auto-triggered when the info email template is sent from the CRM).

cells: Additional sample reports. Attach: residential, commercial, gutter samples. Subject/body TBD by manager.
"Hey, it's {{sender_name}} at FirstMate. Just sent you over a second email with some other sample reports. Did that email go through?"
Follow-up call to check if the info went through.

items.text: Exit: At any point, if the prospect confirms the info went through, the SDR changes the stage to "Info Received," which stops this sequence and starts the Info Received sequence.
Trigger: Lead stage changes to "Info Received."

cells: "Hi {{contact_first_name}}, here are a few other sample reports so you can check these out as well. I attached a residential house with a gutter report add-on, a multi-family apartment building, and a commercial building that's part flat and part sloped so you can see what that looks like as well. Please let me know if you have any questions or want me to help you walk through signing up for the platform." Attach: residential + gutter combo, multi-family, commercial (flat/sloped).
"Hey, just sent you over a few more samples so you can see a couple different options and versions of what the report looks like for different types of roofs. Let me know if you want to sign up."
Call to follow up on samples.

"Hey {{contact_first_name}}, wanted to see if you got a second to check out those samples. I'm here if you have any questions. Here's the link again to save you a search: FirstMeasure.com. No rush at all, just didn't want this to get buried in your inbox."

items.text: Exit: If the prospect signs up, the SDR changes the stage to "Signed Up" (or it auto-transitions when a customer account is linked), which stops this sequence and starts the Signed Up sequence.
Trigger: Lead stage changes to "Signed Up."

cells: "Hey {{contact_first_name}}, just saw that you signed up. That's awesome! Let me know if you have any questions - I'm here to help if anything comes up. I'm sometimes on the phone or in meetings, so the fastest response is always going to be from our support team. If you have any technical questions about the reports or using the platform or anything at all, you can reach them at support@1m8.ai. Anyway, just wanted to say welcome!"
Call to check in - signed up but hasn't ordered. See if there are questions or find out why they haven't ordered yet.

"Hey {{contact_first_name}}, just tried to give you a call. Noticed you signed up a couple days ago but haven't placed your first order yet - totally fine, just wanted to check in. Do you have any questions? When do you think you'll put in your first report?"

items.text: Event-based trigger within this sequence:

cells: First report delivered (at any point after signup)
Create follow-up call task: Call to see what they thought of the first report and offer the bonus credits offer for loading their account.
After the first-report follow-up call is marked complete
Send email with the bonus offer details.

items.text: Note: The first-report call should trigger regardless of whether the lead went through the "no order after 2 days" steps. Even if they ordered on day 1, the SDR should call after that first report is delivered back to the customer. All steps auto-pause if the prospect responds at any point (see Stop Conditions).
Trigger: A new customer is assigned to an SDR (even if the signup didn't originate from that SDR's lead - see SDR Assignment below).

cells: Introduction email from the assigned SDR. Content TBD - something like: "Hi {{contact_first_name}}, I'm {{sender_name}} and I'll be your point of contact at FirstMate. Welcome aboard! Let me know if you have any questions."
Introductory call from the assigned SDR.
Call to follow up on first report and offer the bonus credits offer.
If Step 3 follow-up marked complete with no answer

items.text: The CRM needs the ability to assign any customer to an SDR, even if that customer didn't come from that SDR's lead list. This covers:
Organic signups (customer found First Mate on their own, no SDR involved)
Referrals
Signups from marketing campaigns
Reassigning a customer from one SDR to another
How it works:
Manager can assign a customer/lead to any SDR from the lead page or from a customer list view.
When a customer is assigned to an SDR, the "New Signup Assignment" sequence kicks off automatically.
The assigned SDR is the one who gets credit for the account going forward (commissions, analytics, etc.).

subsections.source_title: UI: Sequence Status on Lead Page

items.text: A "Sequence" indicator in the lead page header area (next to company name):
No sequence: Small button: "Start Sequence " (for manual enrollment if needed)
Active sequence: Badge showing sequence name, current step (e.g., "Step 2 of 4"), next action date, and a "Stop" button.
Paused sequence: Badge showing sequence name, "Paused - action required," and a "Resume" button.
Completed sequence: Badge showing sequence name, "Completed" tag, date completed.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-15: The lead Activity schedule bar now saves timed follow-ups back into CRM, records scheduling events in the Activity feed, stores invite/Meet intent in follow-up metadata, and supports the lead/local-time scheduling presentation in the lead page UI. Live Google Calendar availability, attendee invites, Meet creation, and calendar-account sync are still pending.

2026-04-17: Scheduling is now split between CRM-only follow-ups and Google Calendar meetings. The lead scheduler can load day events from the connected Google account, create real calendar events with attendee and Google Meet options, and keep date/time comparisons visible between the rep and lead local time. Daily dashboard surfacing of exact scheduled events is still open.

2026-04-17: Google Calendar is now fully wired into the CRM flow. Lead scheduling can create real Google Calendar events, read day availability, sync cancellation state back into CRM follow-ups, and surface meetings/follow-ups on the new Daily Dashboard and Pipeline operational views.

items.text: The calendar integration enhances the existing follow-up system. When an SDR wants to set a follow-up for a specific time (not just a date), the system shows their Google Calendar so they can pick a time slot, and the event goes directly onto their calendar with the lead details.
Uses the same Google account connection as Gmail. Always uses the SDR's primary calendar only.

subsections.source_title: How It Works: Follow-Up with Time

items.text: The existing follow-up system already lets SDRs set a follow-up for a specific day. The calendar integration adds a time-specific option:
SDR is on the lead page and wants to schedule a callback or meeting.
SDR uses the schedule bar at the top of the Activity panel. Quick-pick options:
Date quick-picks: Tomorrow, 3 Days, Next Week (sets date only, no specific time).

Time block quick-picks: Morning (9:00 AM) and Afternoon (4:00 PM) - standard follow-up blocks that pair with a date. Example: clicking "Tomorrow" then "Morning" creates a follow-up for tomorrow morning. These do NOT create Google Calendar events - they only add the follow-up to the CRM's follow-up list and the Upcoming section on the lead page. On the dashboard, morning and afternoon follow-ups appear in their own grouped sections so the SDR can batch their callbacks.
Custom date: Date picker for any specific date.
Pick a time: Opens the Google Calendar day view for precise time selection (see below).
If the SDR wants a specific time beyond the morning/evening blocks, they click "Pick a time."
This opens a view of their Google Calendar for that day, showing their existing events so they can see when they're free.
SDR clicks an open time slot (or manually enters a time).
A calendar event is created with the following details:
Calendar event fields:

cells: Selected from the calendar view. Shows both the SDR's local time and the lead's local time side by side (e.g., "2:00 PM PT / 5:00 PM ET") so the SDR can confidently say "I'll call you at 5pm your time."
15 min, 30 min, or 1 hour. Default: 15 min.
Optional. SDR can add notes about what to discuss. Pre-fills with the lead's CRM URL and the company phone number.

items.text: The event is created on the SDR's Google Calendar.
A follow-up record is created in the CRM (linked to the lead) with the specific date AND time, marked as "scheduled."
The event appears in the lead's Activity feed as "Follow-up scheduled."
On the SDR's daily dashboard, this follow-up shows up in their list of scheduled activities for the day with the exact time.
The SDR should be able to choose between three modes when creating a time-specific follow-up:
1. Personal reminder (default): Just put it on the SDR's calendar. The prospect is not notified. This is for "call them back at 2pm" type follow-ups.

2. Send calendar invite to prospect (optional): Add one or more of the lead's contacts as attendees on the calendar event. The prospect receives a calendar invitation via email. Good for scheduled phone calls or demos where both parties need to be available.
SDR toggles "Invite contact" on.
Selects which contact(s) from the lead to add (autocomplete from lead's contacts, uses their email addresses).
The Google Calendar invite is sent to those contacts.
3. Google Meet meeting (optional): Same as option 2, but also adds a Google Meet video link to the calendar event. Good for screen-share demos or virtual meetings.
SDR toggles "Add Google Meet" on.
A Meet link is automatically generated and included in the calendar invite.
The Meet link is also saved in the CRM follow-up record so it's accessible from the lead page and the daily dashboard.
Note: Options 2 and 3 are nice-to-haves. If they add too much complexity for the initial release, ship option 1 only (personal calendar reminder) and add attendee invites and Google Meet later.
No Google account connected: Show prompt to connect. The "Pick a time" option is disabled; SDRs can still set date-only follow-ups without the calendar integration.
Meeting cancelled in Google Calendar: The CRM follow-up remains until manually marked done. (Future: sync cancellations.)
When a caller opens the CRM (not on a specific lead), they see a dashboard showing what they need to do today. Inspired by Ashby's interview dashboard.
Top section - "Today" cards:

cells: Calendar events where the customer was invited (via "Invite contacts" or Google Meet). Shows: time, company name, contact name. Click to jump to lead page.

Incoming emails and SMS that the SDR hasn't read yet. Shows: count badge (red if any), sender, subject/preview, timestamp. Click to jump to lead page and auto-mark as read. This ensures no inbound prospect response gets missed.
Follow-ups scheduled for the morning block (9 AM). Overdue items at the top with a red divider. Shows: company name, description. Click to jump to lead page.
Follow-ups scheduled for the afternoon/evening block (4 PM). Same format as morning.
Follow-ups with specific times (from calendar) or date-only follow-ups.
General to-do items for the day (e.g., "Upload Orum CSV," "Review cold leads," custom tasks). SDRs and managers can create tasks. Not tied to a specific lead. Checkable to mark complete.

items.text: The distinction: a "meeting" is a follow-up where the customer was invited. Morning/afternoon follow-ups are personal reminders that do NOT create calendar events - they just appear in the follow-up list and the Upcoming section on the lead page.
Bottom section - "My Pipeline":
A full-width pipeline section below the leaderboard showing leads that need attention. A toggle at the top switches between two views:

cells: Leads at Info Sent or Info Received with recent activity (contact within the last 7 days). These are actively being worked and close to converting. Sorted by most recent activity. Badge shows count.

Leads at Info Sent or Info Received with no contact in over 7 days. These need immediate attention before they go stale. Sorted by longest time since last contact (coldest first). Red indicator showing days since last contact. Badge shows count.

items.text: These lists can be long (50-100+ leads). The section is full-width and scrollable with no max-height - the full list renders on the page. Each row shows: company name, stage badge (Info Sent / Info Received), and days since last contact. Click to jump to lead page.
Manager view: Sees all reps' hot and cold leads, filterable by rep. Useful for coaching - "Hey, you have 8 leads going cold, let's prioritize those today."
This section can also be accessed as its own "Pipeline" page from the sidebar for a full-screen view with more filters and sorting options.
Middle section - "Leaderboard":
The leaderboard sits below the today cards. It should feel dynamic - rankings visibly update as SDRs work, so people can see themselves and others moving up and down.
Time toggle: A toggle at the top to switch between Today and This Week (Monday through Sunday of the current week - not a rolling 7 days). Default: Today.
Leaderboard columns:

cells: Number of leads moved to "Info Sent" stage
Number of leads moved to "Info Received" stage
Number of leads that signed up (moved to "Signed Up" stage)
Number of accounts that took the bonus offer (loaded $500+ via one of the bonus tiers within 24 hours of first report delivery)
Total dollar value of those funding transactions

items.text: Sorting: Every column is sortable. Click a column header to sort by that column. Default sort: Info Sent, descending.
Dynamic updates: The leaderboard should update in near real-time so SDRs can see rankings shift as the day progresses. This is one of the main motivational tools for the team.
Callers see their own full stats and the leaderboard (summary only - no clicking into other callers' details).
Managers see everything plus can click any caller to drill into their detailed analytics (Module 11).

implementation_notes: 2026-04-17: The Daily Dashboard and full Pipeline view are now live in the sales portal. They render real meetings, unread email/SMS, morning/afternoon/other follow-ups, tasks, leaderboard stats, and hot/cold pipeline rows with lead deep-links and Google Calendar-backed meeting visibility.

2026-04-15: A mockup-parity Tools drawer now renders directly inside the lead page shell with Scripts, Calculator, and Comparison tabs so the front end matches the design. Real data wiring and final behavior for those tabs still need implementation in later passes.
