items.text: The existing scripts drawer is expanded into a Tools drawer - a slide-out panel on the right side of the lead page that contains everything an SDR needs at their fingertips during a call: scripts, the savings calculator, and competitor comparison info.

The current scripts drawer behavior stays the same (floating right-side panel, resizable, push content left when open), but it's renamed to "Tools" and now contains multiple sections the SDR can switch between.
"Tools" button in the lead page header (replaces the current "Scripts" floating button). Clicking it opens/closes the drawer.
Inside the drawer - tabs or sections:

cells: Exactly what exists today - quick-select buttons across the top, full script body below. Manager-created, rich text. No changes to current functionality.

items.text: Nice-to-have - not critical for initial launch. The savings calculator is rebuilt as a component inside the tools drawer. The SDR fills it out live on the call.
Inputs:

cells: Dropdown: EagleView, QuickMeasure, Roofr, RoofScope, Other, None.
Pre-fills based on selected provider's known pricing (if available), or SDR enters manually.

items.text: Output:
Monthly and annual cost with current provider
Monthly and annual cost with First Mate
Monthly and annual savings
Price per report comparison

Nice-to-have - not critical for initial launch. When a provider is selected in the calculator, the comparison tab shows a breakdown of First Mate vs. that specific provider. This includes feature differences, pricing differences, turnaround time, report quality notes - whatever is relevant for the sales conversation.
This content is static/manager-configured (not dynamically generated). The manager maintains comparison data for each competitor.
Everything the SDR enters in the tools drawer is automatically saved as a note on the lead. This happens when the SDR switches tabs or closes the drawer.
The saved note includes:
Provider selected (e.g., "Current provider: EagleView")
Volume (e.g., "Reports per week: 10")
Calculated savings (e.g., "Annual savings: $X,XXX")
Timestamp

This data shows up in the lead's Activity feed as a note (e.g., "Calculator: EagleView, 10 reports/week, $X,XXX annual savings"). The calculator fields reset each time - if the SDR needs to reference previous inputs, they check the notes.
It would be useful but not a major requirement if the tools drawer also had a tab that showed a shortlist of our most active customers that are near to the current prospect.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-17: Tracker updated to reflect that the core stage model, milestone model, automatic forward transitions, and the Info Sent -> Mark Info Received workflow are live. Manager-configurable stage settings and the dedicated manager pipeline board are still pending.

2026-04-17: Dedicated Pipeline and Sequences tabs are now live, the stage board opens leads directly, inbound email/SMS/RingCentral call activity can auto-advance Info Sent -> Info Received, and Do Not Contact dispositions now force the DNC stage. Automatic Account Funded / 10 Orders milestone detection still remains future work.

items.text: Every lead has a stage (where they are in the process) and milestones (independent goals to hit). Stages are linear. Milestones are checkboxes that can be completed in any order.
Stages are defined at the company level by the manager. They represent where the lead is in the sales process.
Default stages:

cells: At least one dial attempt made
SDR sent the initial info email with signup instructions (auto-triggered when the info email template is sent)
Prospect confirmed they received the info email and signup instructions
Prospect created a First Mate account
Prospect is using the product (placing orders)
Prospect declined or went with a competitor

items.text: Manager can add/edit/reorder stages from a settings page. "Lost" and "Do Not Contact" are terminal stages.
Milestones track specific goals the SDR needs to push for after signup. They are independent - a lead can complete them in any order, or complete one without the other.

cells: Prospect took the bonus offer - funded their account via one of the bonus tiers within 24 hours of their first report delivery.
Detected from Stripe transaction records. Bonus credits added by the system as part of the offer do not count toward the $500+ threshold - only the customer's actual payment.
Prospect has placed 10 actual orders. Fully activated.
Can be detected automatically from the linked customer account's lifetime order count.

items.text: Stage indicator displayed prominently in the lead page header, next to the company name. Shows the current stage as a colored badge/pill.
Stage selector: Clicking the badge opens a dropdown to manually change the stage. Auto-saves on selection. Stage change is logged in the Activity feed ("Moved from X to Y by [rep name]").
Displayed near the stage badge in the lead page header, or in a small section just below the header fields.
Two checkboxes with labels: "Account Funded" and "10 Orders."
Checkboxes can be checked automatically by the system (when detected from the linked account data) or manually by the SDR.

Visual indicator if a milestone is overdue - e.g., if "Account Funded" is unchecked and the lead's first report was delivered more than 24 hours ago, show it highlighted in red/orange with a label like "Bonus offer expired."
Some stage changes happen automatically:

cells: First Orum dial event imported for this lead
Any of the 5 email templates sent from CRM to this lead
Lead replies to an email (inbound email received while at Info Sent stage)
Customer account gets linked to the lead
First order placed on linked account
DNC disposition set or Do Not Contact flag set

items.text: Note: "Info Received" can also be set manually by the SDR via the "Mark Info Received" banner (for verbal confirmation on the phone). The auto-transition from an email reply handles the case where the prospect responds to the email without calling back.

When a lead is at the Info Sent stage, a full-width blue banner appears at the top of the lead page (below the topbar, above the header): "This lead is at Info Sent - did they confirm receipt?" with a prominent "Mark Info Received" button on the right side. Clicking the button immediately moves the stage to Info Received, stops the Info Sent sequence, starts the Info Received sequence, and dismisses the banner. This should be highly visible - the SDR confirms receipt while still on the phone and needs to do it with one click.
Rules:
Auto-transitions only move a lead forward in the pipeline, never backward.
Manual stage changes by the SDR or manager can move in any direction.
Auto-transitions are logged in the Activity feed as "System" actions.
A new view accessible from the portal sidebar: "Pipeline."
Displays a kanban-style board or table showing lead counts per stage, filterable by assigned caller, list, or date range. Clicking a stage shows the leads in that stage.

Milestone filters: Manager can also filter by milestone status - e.g., "Show me all Signed Up leads where Account Funded is not checked" or "Active Customers with less than 10 orders." This makes it easy to generate lists for targeted outreach (including bulk email via Module 2).
Manager creates or imports lead lists and assigns them to callers. This module already exists and is mostly unchanged, but needs the following additions.
Pull lead lists from Google My Business integration
Manually create lead lists
Assign/reassign lists to callers
SDRs can add individual leads manually from the Leads view. This covers cases where an SDR gets a referral, finds a prospect on their own, or needs to add someone they met at a trade show.
Flow:
SDR clicks "Add Lead" button (visible in the Leads view).
A form opens with fields: company name, phone, email, website, address, and optional notes.
SDR fills in what they have and saves.
The lead is created at "New" stage, assigned to the SDR who created it.
The lead is not associated with any list - it's a standalone lead.

When a customer signs up for First Mate, the system needs to match (pair) their new account to an existing lead in the CRM. The current pairing search is slow - it only accepts one character at a time and the workflow is cumbersome.
Improvements:

Full search: The pairing search must support full text input (type a full company name, not character by character). Search should be fast and fuzzy - matching on company name, phone, email, or website.

Auto-match (4-star): Any match rated 4-star confidence or higher should be paired automatically with no manual review. This drastically reduces the manual matching workload. This could be if any lead matches on more than one variable it gets paired automatically. So contact name to user name, phone number, company name, domain, etc gets matched and the lead that has the most activity is most likely to be paired if there are multiple leads that may be matched.

Manager single-pair: Manager can manually pair one account at a time from either the account list or the lead page. A "Pair Account" button on the lead page opens a search of unmatched customer accounts and lets the manager link one with a click.
Speed: The overall attribution process must run significantly faster than today. Ideally 90% of signups paired within minutes of a new signup.
Managers can import a CSV file to create a new lead list. This is the primary way to get leads into the system outside of Google My Business.
Import flow:
Manager clicks "Import CSV" in the Lead Lists view.
File picker opens. Manager selects a CSV.
CRM shows a column mapping screen - the manager maps CSV columns to lead fields (company name, phone, email, address, website, etc.). The system should auto-detect common column names.
Manager names the list and confirms.
Leads are created and added to the new list. Each lead gets a CRM callback URL auto-generated for Orum export.

Duplicate handling: If a lead with the same phone number or company name + address already exists in the system, flag it during import preview so the manager can decide whether to skip or create a new record.
List progress tracking: After the daily Orum CSV import, the system calculates how many leads on each list have been called. The manager can see:
List name
Assigned caller
Total leads
Leads called
Leads remaining
Percent complete
Estimated "runs out" time (based on caller's average pace, if data available)
Threshold alerts: If a caller's list is  85% called through, the manager gets a notification (delivery method TBD - see TODO).

Dialer URL generation: When a list is created or imported, each lead's CRM callback URL is auto-generated and included in the export format that Orum expects. The manager should be able to export a list as an Orum-ready CSV with one click.

Filtered export / custom call lists (LOW PRIORITY): When viewing a lead list, the manager can filter leads by call history and disposition, then export only the filtered results as an Orum-ready CSV. This allows the manager to build targeted re-dial lists.
Filter options:
Called but no conversation (dialed, but no call over 1 minute)
Gatekeeper reached previously
Decision maker reached previously
Called but gave an objection last time
Any combination of the above
This is a lower-priority feature. The core list management (import, assign, export, progress tracking) should ship first.

implementation_notes: 2026-04-17: Lead list management is now live end-to-end, including manual list creation, CSV import and mapping, assignment/reassignment, list progress metrics, filtered selected-list browsing, and Orum-ready export flows for both whole lists and filtered lead selections.

items.text: At the end of each day, the manager downloads the Orum activity CSV and uploads it to the CRM. The CRM parses the CSV, matches records to leads, and updates call history. This flow already exists and works fine - no major changes needed.
Manager clicks "Import Orum Data" in the portal.
File picker opens. Manager selects the CSV.
CRM parses the CSV and shows a preview: total rows, matched to existing leads, unmatched.
Manager confirms import.
Call history records are created for each matched row. Unmatched rows are logged for review.
After import, list progress stats (Module 9) are recalculated.
If the same call data is imported again (e.g., re-uploading yesterday's CSV), duplicates should not be created.
Both SDRs and managers have access to the Analytics page, but with different scopes. SDRs see only their own detailed analytics. Managers see team-level data and can drill into any individual rep.

Important distinction: The daily dashboard leaderboard (Module 6) is where everyone sees everyone's summary stats. The Analytics page is for detailed breakdowns - reps see only their own, managers see everyone.
Accessed from the portal sidebar: "Analytics."
Time toggle: Day | Week | Month
Main graph showing the following metrics as lines or bars, plotted over the selected time range:

cells: Past days only (from Orum import - not available for current day)
Past days only (from Orum import - not available for current day)

items.text: How the time toggle affects the graph:
Day (current day): Shows the current day by hour. Only shows Info Sent, Info Received, Sign-Ups, Accounts Funded, and 10-Order Milestones (no call data since Orum hasn't been imported yet).
Day (past day): Shows that day by hour. Includes all metrics including Calls Made and Conversations from the Orum import.
Week: Shows each day as a data point. Week starts Monday.
Month: Shows each day as a data point for the selected month.
The SDR can toggle individual metrics on/off on the graph to focus on specific ones.
The manager sees everything the SDR sees, plus:
Team-level graph: Same metrics as above, but aggregated across all SDRs (or a filtered set). This is the default view when the manager opens Analytics.
Rep selector: Dropdown to select an individual rep and view their graph. Can also multi-select reps to compare them on the same graph.
Filters:
Date range picker
Rep filter (dropdown, multi-select)
List filter (dropdown, multi-select)
The manager can compare current performance against the equivalent previous period to see if the team is trending up or down.
How it works:
Daily view: Compare today (by hour) against yesterday, or the same day last week. Example: "It's 2 PM Tuesday - last Tuesday at 2 PM we had 4 sign-ups, today we have 6. We're tracking 50% ahead."
Weekly view: Compare this week (Mon-current day) against last week (same days). Example: "Through Wednesday this week we have 12 Info Sent. Through Wednesday last week we had 9. Up 33%."
Monthly view: Compare this month (through today) against last month (through same date).

Display: Each metric in the summary cards and pipeline table shows the current value plus a comparison indicator: " 33% vs last week" (green) or " 15% vs last week" (red). The graph can overlay the previous period as a faded/dashed line behind the current period so the manager can visually see how the team is pacing.

Per-rep or team: The comparison works at both the team aggregate level and the individual rep level. Manager can toggle between "Team" and a specific rep to see if that individual is ahead or behind their own previous pace.

Hourly pacing (daily view): On the day view, the graph shows data by hour. A projected trendline (dashed) can extend to end-of-day based on the current pace, so the manager can estimate: "At this rate, we'll finish the day with ~8 sign-ups vs 6 yesterday."
The manager can view analytics broken down by state (based on lead addresses) to see how different geographic regions are performing.
State-level metrics:

cells: Number of leads in that state
How many leads in that state moved to Info Sent
How many moved to Info Received
Info Sent  Info Received  Sign-Up  Funded as percentages

items.text: This helps the manager see which states/regions are performing well and which ones need different approaches or more attention. Can be viewed as a table sorted by any column.

Below the graph, both SDRs and managers see a table view showing pipeline stats with conversion percentages between each stage. Similar in format to the Orum rep performance table, but using our sales pipeline stages instead of call metrics.
Columns (SDR sees their own row; manager sees all reps):

cells: Total leads assigned to this rep
Number of leads that reached Contacted stage
Info Sent / Contacted (conversion from previous stage)
Total dollar value of funding transactions

items.text: Each percentage cell should be color-coded (green for strong conversion, red for weak) so it's easy to spot at a glance where leads are dropping off - both for individual reps and across the team.
Sortable by any column. Respects the same Day/Week/Month time toggle as the graph above.
Manager sees all reps as rows plus a "Team Total" row at the top or bottom showing aggregated numbers.
These are recommendations - not explicitly requested but would add value:
Average time between stages: How many days on average from Info Sent to Info Received? From Sign-Up to Account Funded? This shows pipeline velocity and where things stall.
Sequence effectiveness: For each sequence, what percentage of enrolled leads hit the next stage? Are the sequences actually working?

The commissions system has now been overhauled around real derived commission events instead of the old milestone-only model. Revenue sync now uses persisted Stripe payment records and Stripe auto-topups instead of internal credit-balance changes, milestone payout is configurable per SDR, payroll/export flows are live, and the commission layer supports milestone, bonus-offer, referral-signup, and referral-bonus event types. The customer-facing bonus/referral program flows are still tracked separately in Modules 16 and 17, so this module remains in progress until those upstream flows are fully closed.
Every customer/lead can have an assigned SDR. This is the SDR who gets credit (and commission) for that account.
By default, the assigned SDR is whoever was working the lead when they signed up.
Managers can reassign any customer to a different SDR at any time. This covers organic signups, referrals, marketing signups, and team rebalancing.
When a customer is reassigned, the new SDR's "New Signup Assignment" sequence (Module 4) kicks off automatically.
The assigned SDR is shown on the lead page and in customer lists.

Existing model, largely unchanged. When a customer's cumulative order revenue hits a threshold (currently $70), the assigned SDR earns a one-time commission payout. One milestone per customer maximum - once a customer crosses $70, the SDR earns the payout and no further milestone commissions are earned on that customer.
What's changing:

The payout amount per milestone is now configurable per-SDR by the manager. Currently it's a flat $10 for everyone. The manager should be able to set a different payout amount for each SDR (e.g., $10 for one rep, $15 for another).
The milestone threshold ($70) remains company-wide for now.
What counts as revenue:

Only actual Stripe transactions count. If credits are added to a customer's account as a bonus, promotion, or manual adjustment (not through a Stripe payment), they do NOT count toward the revenue milestone.
The system must pull revenue from Stripe payment records, not from the credits balance.

Reassignment rule: If a customer is assigned to an SDR after the customer has already signed up, the revenue milestone commission does NOT apply. The milestone commission is only earned by the SDR who was assigned when the customer originally signed up and reached $70 in spend.

5% commission on the customer's bonus offer payment. The SDR earns 5% of whatever the customer pays (not the bonus credits - the actual Stripe charge) when the customer takes one of the bonus offer tiers within the bonus window.
How it works:
Customer's first report is delivered. This starts a 24-hour bonus offer window.
During that window, the customer sees a popup and persistent banner in the First Mate portal presenting the bonus offer tiers (see Bonus Offer section below).
If the customer takes any tier, the SDR earns 5% of the customer's actual payment.
Example: Customer takes Tier 2 ($1,000 payment, gets $500 bonus). SDR earns 5% of $1,000 = $50.
Example: Customer takes Tier 4 (custom $5,000 payment, gets $2,500 bonus). SDR earns 5% of $5,000 = $250.
Only the actual Stripe payment counts. The bonus credits are not included in the commission calculation.

SDR extension: If the bonus offer expires (24 hours passed) but the customer still wants to fund, the SDR can manually approve a late bonus offer from the lead page. The SDR clicks an "Extend Bonus Offer" button, which reopens the window for that customer and preserves the SDR's commission eligibility. This handles cases where the customer was on the phone with the SDR a day or two later and is ready to load up. Manager can see all extensions in analytics.

Reassignment rule: The bonus offer commission does apply even if the customer was assigned to the SDR after signup. If a new customer is assigned to an SDR and that customer takes the bonus offer within the window, the SDR earns the commission.

Possible simplification: To make commission tracking easier, the SDR could simply earn 5% on any Stripe payment over $500 made within 3 days of the first report delivery - regardless of whether the customer used the bonus offer or not. The customer still sees the bonus offer as a 24-hour window, but the SDR's commission window is quietly wider. This eliminates the need for the "Extend Bonus Offer" mechanism for commission purposes (the extend button would still exist for giving the customer the bonus credits). Simpler to track, fewer edge cases.

SDRs earn a $10 flat commission for every new customer signup that was referred by one of their assigned customers. Additionally, the SDR earns 5% of the bonus offer payment for referred signups - same structure as Commission Type 2, but for customers they didn't cold-call.
How it works:
SDR's customer (the referrer) shares their referral link.
A new customer signs up through that link.
The SDR who owns the referrer's account earns $10 when the referred customer signs up.
If the referred customer also takes the bonus offer, the SDR earns 5% of that payment too.
This incentivizes SDRs to push the referral program during their calls and follow-ups.

Every new customer gets a one-time bonus offer that activates when their first report is delivered. The offer expires 24 hours after delivery. The goal is to get customers to load a significant balance immediately, which increases stickiness and lifetime value.
In the first report delivery email:
The report delivery email includes a section promoting the bonus offer with all four tiers.
Clear call-to-action button: "Claim Your Signup Bonus" linking to the portal.
SDR notification:
When the first report is delivered, the SDR receives an email notification: "First report delivered for [Company Name] - bonus offer window is now open (24 hours)."
This also triggers the appropriate sequence step in the CRM (see Module 4), creating a follow-up call task for the SDR to call the customer and pitch the bonus offer live.
Portal popup (customer-facing):
When the customer logs into the First Mate portal after their first report is delivered, they see a modal popup presenting the bonus offer with all four tiers.
Each tier has a clear "Select" button that takes them to checkout.
The popup can be closed.

First-login reset: If no user on the account has logged in since the first report was delivered, the 24-hour countdown starts from their first login, not from delivery time. This ensures the customer always gets the full 24 hours to see and act on the offer, even if they don't log in for days. The SDR notification email still fires on delivery so the SDR can call and pitch it.
Portal banner (customer-facing):
Once the customer closes the popup, a persistent banner appears at the top of the portal with a countdown timer showing time remaining in the 24-hour window.
Banner copy: something like " Signup bonus: Load your account and get up to 50% in bonus credits! [Time remaining: 18h 42m] - Claim Now"
The banner remains visible on every page until the offer expires or is claimed.
After the bonus offer expires (24 hours):
The popup and countdown banner are removed.
Replaced by the referral program prompt (see below).
If the 24-hour window expires but the customer still wants to take the offer:
The SDR can click an "Extend Bonus Offer" button on the lead page in the CRM.
This reopens the bonus offer window for that specific customer (resets the 24-hour countdown).
The SDR still earns commission on extended offers.
Extensions are logged in the Activity feed and visible to managers in analytics.

Maximum extension: The bonus offer can only be extended up to 3 business days after the first report delivery. After that, the offer cannot be extended regardless. This prevents indefinite extensions while giving the SDR a reasonable window to close.

Since the SDRs will be calling these customers as part of the bonus sign-up sequence, it would be cool if there was some sort of notification to tell the SDRs when the user logs on to FirstMate. They can call them when they know they are available and have us on their mind because they are ordering a report.
While we're at it in the pop-up and email we should add a call us button that would go to the SDR that's assigned to the account. If they have questions about the offer they can call them directly

The referral program encourages existing customers to refer other roofing companies to First Mate. Referrals are tracked per individual user (not per company), and each user gets their own unique referral link.

cells: $100 digital Visa gift card, sent to their email
Nothing - no incentive for the new customer
$10 commission + 5% of referred customer's bonus offer payment

items.text: Gift card trigger: The $100 gift card is sent to the referrer's direct email once the referred customer has spent $500 on any First Mate products (cumulative Stripe revenue, not bonus credits).

Gift card fulfillment: Automated via a gift card API (e.g., Tremendous, Sendoso, or similar). When the $500 threshold is met, the system auto-triggers the gift card delivery to the referrer's email. No manual intervention needed.
Each individual user (not company) gets a unique referral link (not a referral code).
Any signup through that link is automatically marked as a referral in the system, attributed to both the referring user and the SDR who owns the referring user's account.
The referral link is persistent - it doesn't expire.

subsections.source_title: Referral Collision (Lead Already Exists in CRM)

items.text: If a new customer signs up through a referral link, but that company already exists in the CRM as a lead being worked by a different SDR:
Both SDRs earn the $10 flat referral commission. The cold-call SDR (lead owner) gets $10 and the referral SDR (who owns the referring customer) gets $10.
Only the lead owner gets the 5% bonus offer commission. Whichever SDR owns the lead is the one who earns 5% on the bonus offer payment. The referral SDR does not earn the 5% in a collision scenario.
The cold-call SDR also earns their standard milestone commission when the customer hits $70 revenue.
The lead stays assigned to the original cold-call SDR - referral attribution doesn't change lead ownership.
The referral is still tracked and the referring customer still gets their $100 gift card.

There is no cap on referral commissions or bonus offer commissions. If one company's users generate many referrals, the SDR earns on all of them uncapped. This incentivizes SDRs to actively push the referral program with their most engaged customers.
24 hours after the bonus offer expires (which itself is 24 hours after first login - so effectively 48 hours after first login), the referral program is introduced:
Popup: Customer sees a popup explaining the referral program. "Refer a friend to First Mate and receive a $100 Visa gift card after they spend $500."
Persistent banner (forever): After closing the popup, a permanent banner appears on the portal: "Refer a friend and receive a $100 gift card after they spend $500. [Your Referral Link] - Copy"
Email: Customer receives an email explaining the referral program, including their unique referral link.
The banner remains on the portal permanently and is never removed.
On the lead page, the Referrals sub-section in Company Info shows:
How many referrals this company's users have generated.
Which companies were referred and their status (signed up, active, spent $500+, gift card sent).
This data is imported via daily CSV (see TODO) and displayed as a read-only section.
For each SDR, the manager can set:

cells: Target number of revenue milestones to hit per month
Dollar amount earned per revenue milestone (was previously $10 flat for everyone)

items.text: Semi-monthly pay periods: 1st-15th and 16th-end of month.
First period of the month includes base pay + previous month's commissions (milestones + bonus offer commissions + referral commissions).
Second period is base pay only.
Manager manually marks each payroll row as "completed" when paid.

SDR view: Current month milestone count vs quota, commission earned (milestones + bonus offer commissions + referral commissions), and payroll history. SDR can see their attributed customers, referral signups, and the milestone/bonus/referral detail for each.
Manager view: Full team overview - all SDRs' milestone counts, commission earned, payroll status. Can drill into individual SDR detail and export commission reports.
Accessed from: Portal sidebar under "Commissions."

The current system's milestone sync is broken. Orders and revenue are not pulling into the commission system correctly, which means SDRs see an empty commissions dashboard. This must be fixed as part of the overhaul. The revenue data source must be actual Stripe transaction records tied to customer orgs, not internal credit balance changes.
Contacts: short notes display. The current contacts section shows "No short notes yet" even when a contact has a short note. This needs to be fixed.

Commission: revenue data sync. Resolved on 2026-04-20 by replacing the broken milestone sync with Stripe-payment-based commission attribution and refreshed commission reporting. Keep this entry only as historical context for the overhaul in Module 12.
Attribution: speed and auto-matching. See Lead-to-Account Pairing section in Module 9. The current process is too slow and 4-star matches should auto-pair.
